ch26.note: The Central Reserve Bank of China (中央储备银行), the bank of Wang Jingwei's puppet regime, opened in 1941. Its 'reserve notes' were the occupation currency forced on the areas Japan held, set up to drive out the Nationalists' fabi—which is why the bank and its men were targets.

Not the Christian sense: this is the Chinese custom of fictive kinship (干亲), by which one formally takes another as adoptive 'godmother' or 'goddaughter' to bind two families together or to place a young woman under a powerful protector—a tie of obligation without blood or religion.

ch26.anchor: the Pearl Harbor affair of December 8, 1941
ch26.note: Across the international date line the attack on Pearl Harbor, dated 7 December in the United States, fell on 8 December in East Asia. That same morning Japanese troops marched into the foreign concessions of Shanghai, ending the 'solitary island' years and the shelter they had given.

Zikawei (Xujiahui), the old Jesuit and French Catholic quarter in the southwest of Shanghai, centered on the twin-spired St. Ignatius Cathedral—a conspicuous landmark used here to fix the scene of an operation.
The 'great rear' (大后方) was unoccupied Nationalist China—the interior behind the fighting front, centered on the wartime capital Chongqing—as against the Japanese-held 'fallen zones' along the coast.

ch26.anchor: old Wang praising his own melons
ch26.note: From the saying 'Old Wang selling melons cries up his own wares' (老王卖瓜，自卖自夸), for shameless self-promotion. This 'Wang' is the proverbial melon-seller, not Wang Jingwei.
